children: The Investment & Development Conversations session, titled ‘Funding India's Hospitality Decade: Capital, Confidence & Partnerships’, brought together leaders from hotel development, investments, private equity and hospitality companies to examine the forces influencing investment decisions across the sector

The 10th edition of the prestigious BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026), hosted at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity, is bringing leading voices from across the hospitality industry for the next two days of conversations on the sector’s growth and evolution. With the theme
‘India’s Hospitality Decade: From Growth to Greatness’
, the Summit will examine the opportunities, challenges and shifts shaping India’s hospitality landscape as the industry enters a defining decade.

As India’s hospitality sector entered a period of continued development, the availability and deployment of capital became increasingly important to determining where and how the next phase of growth would take shape. The
‘Funding India's Hospitality Decade: Capital, Confidence & Partnerships’
, brought together leaders from hotel development, investments, private equity and hospitality companies to examine the forces influencing investment decisions across the sector.
Rajneesh Malhotra, Country Head - Hospitality, Asset Management & Business Development, Adani Realty

Anika Gupta, Senior VP – Development & Brand Leader, amã, Indian Hotels Company Ltd (IHCL); Gyana Das, EVP & Head of Investments, SAMHI Hotels; Mohit Arora, MD, Blackstone, Mumbai; and Shwetank Singh, MD & CEO, Chalet Hotels Limited

Gupta explained, “The path to development or growth will be two-pronged. One is going to be traditional, where we’ll continue with densification of core networks, and the other will be where people discover and keep discovering new destinations. Development is going to happen at multiple levels, through multiple geographies and through multiple products. It’s not just going to remain a universe of hospitality; it will actually become a multiverse, because there’ll be different universes operating within it”.
Das explained, “We buy what we want to buy. Investment analysis starts at the beginning. We have a list of macro markets, which is revised regularly.”

Arora said, “Amongst all asset classes, hotels are the top. As Indians, our income levels are going up and we want to travel on every occasion, and with that the demand is going up. But the supply is less. You can price every day, and that is the best part.”
Singh added, “Hospitality is not a game for the weak-hearted.”

The session wrapped up with a practical focus on what it takes to secure institutional capital for Indian hospitality. The panel made it clear that attracting long-term funding requires moving past speculative projections, standardising investment frameworks, and structuring owner-operator partnerships that offer clear risk protection alongside healthy returns.

The two-day BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) encompasses over 25 sessions where hospitality veterans and experts across the nation gathered to provide diverse knowledge and insights. The Summit & Awards is a testament to BW Hotelier’s commitment towards revolutionising Indian hospitality by honouring the crème de la crème of the industry.
